ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A student investigates the state change characteristics of an ideal gas within a closed cylinder, and obtains the variation of pressure $p$ with temperature $t$ as shown in the figure. It is known that curve I describes an isochoric process with a volume of $V_{1}$, where the pressure of the gas is $p_{1}$ at temperature $t_{1}$; curve II describes an isobaric process with a pressure of $p_{2}$. Take $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ as 273K.

1. Calculate the pressure of the gas at $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ during the isochoric process.
2. The volume of the gas at $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ during the isobaric process.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The accompanying figure is a p-t graph, the vertical axis is labeled p/Pa, the horizontal axis is labeled t/°C, and the origin is O. Curve I in the figure is an inclined straight line in which the pressure p increases as the temperature t increases; the blue dashed line marks the state point on curve I where the temperature is t1, and its corresponding pressure is labeled p1. Curve II is a horizontal straight line, corresponding to the constant pressure p2. Reasoning: The temperature must be converted into thermodynamic temperature. t1°C corresponds to T1 = t1 + 273, and 0°C corresponds to T0 = 273 K. Curve I is an isochoric process with volume V1, and for the same ideal gas p/T is constant, so p0/273 = p1/(t1 + 273), giving p0 = 273p1/(t1 + 273). At 0°C, the state on curve I is (p0, V1, 273K), and the state on curve II is (p2, V2, 273K). For the same gas and the same temperature, from the ideal gas state equation pV = nRT, p0V1 = p2V2 is obtained, therefore V2 = p0V1/p2 = 273p1V1/[p2(t1 + 273)].
